newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus Popular plans Greek expansion.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus Popular plans Greek expansion.

text.p: The Cyprus Popular Bank is launching an expansion programme focused on Greece, where it expects to double its branches within two years, the bank said on Wednesday.

"The European Popular bank (subsidiary) developed in the four years of its existence a network of nine branches in Greece and that is expected to double in the next one or two years," said Kikis Lazarides, the group chief executive of Popular Bank.
Lazarides told the annual meeting in Nicosia that a new branch will open soon in London, bringing the number of branches there to six.
The bank - Cyprus's second largest - posted pre-tax profits of 27.6 million pounds ($54.2 million) in 1996, up 6.2 percent on 1995. Operating profits were up 11.1 percent to 36.8 million pounds.
A 12 percent dividend to shareholders was approved, in addition to the interim dividend of 8 percent paid in October 1996.
Lazarides said the island's economy, which relies heavily on tourism, did not live up to expectations in 1996.
Tourism, which contributes 22 percent to the gross national product, was down by around three percent, according to the most-recent official estimates.
"A restrictive environment prevailed (in 1996) and this affected the activities of commercial banks," said Lazarides.
"Taking that into account the results of the Group are considered very satisfactory," he said.
Profit from overseas activities grew to 16 percent of overall operating profit in 1996 from 10 percent in 1995.
An economic slowdown in 1996 resulted in a GDP growth of around two percent for Cyprus, he said.
The Finance Ministry's most recent projections put GDP growth at a provisional 1.9 percent in 1996 from a provisional 6.0 percent growth in 1995.

Political tension and uncertainty, a restrictive credit policy adopted by the central bank in the first half of 1996 and one of the most severe droughts Cyprus has suffered this century had a negative impact on the economic climate, he said.
The ministry forecasts GDP growth in the region of 3.2 percent in 1997. Lazarides said he would not venture a guess on the economic performance of 1997.

But he said that an improved economic climate in Europe and the strength of the pound sterling against the Cyprus pound is expected to have a favourable impact. Britain is an important market for sales of holiday tours to Cyprus. ($=0.508 pounds)
